result.title: Encoded but Disconnected: Decomposing Vision-Language Model Failures under a Patching Null
result.summary: Across three vision-language model architectures (LLaVA-1.5-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B), we report a universal negative finding for mid-layer interpretability. On POPE -- the benchmark common to all three -- the mid layers encode the ground-truth answer in 68-91% of errors, yet this signal is not causally active for the final prediction: residual-stream patching yields 0% non-trivial flip at the layer level on all three architectures, and on two of three at the per-head level (Qwen: 0/12,600 patched forwards). The lone exception, InternVL3 layer-20 head-2, is a non-vocab, self-attending head whose effect is localized to that specific head (p < 1e-4). Despite the null, the errors separate operationally into three failure modes -- Perception Failure, Encoded-but-Disconnected, Prior-Override -- learnable above 60% on all three architectures, and the architecture's prior direction predicts which of two interventions elicits a category-specific response. We report these mitigation effects under oracle labels as evidence the categories are mechanistically real, not as a deployable method.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在三种 VLM 上对 POPE 错误做中层机制分析与残差流 patching，发现中层虽在 68–91% 的错误中编码了正确答案，却对最终预测无因果作用，并将错误操作化为感知失败、编码但断开、先验覆盖三类。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 LVR 的核心问题：内部状态是否保留任务必要信息、以及这些内容是否被答案读取使用；其「编码但因果断开」的负结果对 latent 状态可用性假设构成重要反驳与诊断线索，宜优先核查。
